title: Jev was dethroned, and the StartLux China open-source decision-making model surged to the top spot.
key_facts: StartLux, a Shanghai AI company founded less than five months ago, officially released the open-source StartLux-Decision models on 30 Sep, according to 36Kr.
A decision model picks from options given to it (yes or no, one of three, a grade, a tool) instead of writing text first.
The 27B version scored 63.88 on Decision Index 0.2.1 against 57.91 for the latest Jev (1.13), beating it on 31 of 38 benchmarks; in chess against Jev 1.13 it won 35 of 36 games.
Those results are self-tests by the StartLux team using public tools and a snapshot of the public ranking as of 28 Sep 2026; a separate set of 7 public tests averaged 91.82% accuracy.
Five sizes were released (0.8B, 2B, 4B, 9B and 27B parameters) with quantized files for local use; the 4B version answers three questions at once in about 26 milliseconds on a single H200 GPU.
The company says it took about 3 days from choosing the direction to finishing the first round of development and checking, helped by an AI-assisted research system.
The article says high-risk actions such as payment, deletion and permission changes still need their original confirmation steps.

This time, StartLux's Decision model has launched 5 versions with 0.8B, 2B, 4B, 9B and 27B parameters in one go, and provides quantized models that support local deployment.
why_it_matters_hint: A free, small decision model that runs on a home machine adds a Chinese rival to the Jev decision-model race, but the scores are the company's own.
